football_evidence.question: Can Maryland’s pass rush get to Illinois’ quarterback?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Illinois, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.0 of the 7.4 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Maryland has the ball (big plays on the ground): Maryland’s offense turns 4.9% of its runs into explosive gains, and Illinois’ defense gives up explosive gains on 4.2% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).

When Illinois has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Illinois’ offense is stopped at or behind the line on 11.6% of its runs, and Maryland’s defense stops 14.2% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Illinois’ quarterback room No. 19 nationally and Maryland’s No. 84.
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Illinois’ offensive line No. 49 nationally and Maryland’s No. 109.
contradicting: When Maryland has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Maryland’s offense has allowed a sack on 2.5% of its dropbacks, and Illinois’ defense sacks the quarterback on 1.8% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Illinois has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Illinois’ offense has allowed a sack on 4.0% of its dropbacks, and Maryland’s defense sacks the quarterback on 9.2% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
In his last two games (Purdue and Michigan State), Houser averaged 6.3 yards per attempt, against 8.5 in his four games before that.
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Maryland’s pass defense No. 50 nationally and Illinois’ No. 96.
quarterbacks: Malik Washington has completed 154 of 258 passes (59.7%) for 1,615 yards, 6.3 yards per attempt, 10 touchdowns and 5 interceptions in seven games for Maryland, and has been sacked on 7 of 265 dropbacks.
Katin Houser has completed 122 of 187 passes (65.2%) for 1,440 yards, 7.7 yards per attempt, 12 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in six games for Illinois, and has been sacked on 6 of 193 dropbacks.
Michael Clayton II has completed 18 of 27 passes (66.7%) for 177 yards, 6.6 yards per attempt, 4 touchdowns and no interceptions in two games for Illinois, and has been sacked on 2 of 29 dropbacks.
